name: TraceMem

paper.title: TraceMem: Weaving Narrative Memory Schemata from User Conversational Traces

construction.unit: episode summary (shared) + per-user experience trace; traces clustered into memory-card threads
construction.kept_as: rewritten dated episode narrative + extracted per-user experience traces
construction.processing: one LLM pass per session labels each turn as topic change or development and writes a fact line per turn; LLM summarises each episode; LLM distils each speaker's own experiences from summary + fact lines

organization.structure: per-user memory card: theme > topics > threads, over experience traces; flat episode store beside it
organization.stores: ChromaDB collections per conversation: episodes, semantics, experiences, threads; card JSON files per user

management.operations: PCA + UMAP + HDBSCAN clusters a user's traces into topics (min 5), then each topic into threads (min 2); LLM titles themes, topics and threads
management.forgetting: experience distillation returns N/A for episodes with no personal facts; these are dropped (13-25% of episodes, Table 3)

retrieval.candidates: dense search over episode summaries; separately an LLM reads the chosen user card(s) in full
retrieval.selection: top-K episodes by similarity; LLM returns up to 10 thread ids per user, threads fetched by id
retrieval.budget: K=10 episodes (paper) / 20 (code) + up to 10 threads per chosen user

use.context: episode summaries + joined experience traces of the selected threads
use.reasoning: single answer call with a step-by-step prompt

classify.note: Two paths are merged: episodes come from dense top-K; threads are chosen by an LLM reading the whole card. The card path is the paper's contribution, so it sets the placement.

stages.ingestion: Each session is formatted with numbered turns (image captions inlined) and one LLM call labels every turn as topic change or topic development; the session is cut before each topic change into episodes.
stages.construction: The same call writes a fact line per turn (the 'semantic' representation). An LLM rewrites each episode into an exhaustive dated summary, then, per speaker, distils that speaker's own experiences from the summary and their fact lines into one experience trace (or N/A).
stages.organization: Per user, experience-trace embeddings are clustered twice (PCA, UMAP, HDBSCAN; noise reassigned) into topics and then threads; an LLM titles each topic and the whole theme and writes a title and summary per thread, giving a JSON memory card (theme > topics > threads with ids).
stages.update: Cards are built in a separate pass after all sessions are added; the paper describes no incremental update or conflict handling.
stages.retrieval: An LLM picks which user card(s) the question is about, reads the full card(s) and returns thread ids (10 per user in the code); in parallel the question retrieves the top episode summaries by embedding similarity (K=10 in the paper, 20 in the code).
stages.answer: The answer LLM reads the episode summaries plus, per user, the concatenated experience traces of each selected thread, with rules for resolving relative dates.

summary: Consolidates dialogue into per-user narrative memory cards: episodes are summarised, each speaker's own experiences are distilled, and these traces are clustered into topics and threads that an LLM browses at question time alongside dense-retrieved episodes.
notes: Paper v1 (10 Feb 2026) read from the arXiv PDF; ACM template with placeholder header ('Trovato et al.'), no venue stated, so recorded as a preprint. Appendix prompt figures are images; prompts were read from the code instead. Code checked at commit 1b681ed9 (19 Feb 2026, latest on main). Table 2 backbone labels: the paper's text ties the 0.9019 block to GPT-4o-mini and the 0.9227 block to GPT-4.1-mini; the table itself lists them in that order.

sources.code_note: Commit 1b681ed9 (19 Feb 2026) is the head of main, nine days after paper v1. It ships the LoCoMo add/build/answer scripts and the answer files for both backbones (1,540 questions each), so it is taken as the evaluation code; exact identity with the paper's runs is not stated.

headline: The answer model reads LLM summaries of episodes and LLM-distilled experience traces, never the original turns (which are not stored).
Threads are not retrieved by similarity: an LLM reads the whole user card in its prompt and names thread ids.
The released code retrieves 20 episodes per question; the paper says K = 10.

fields.name: thread title + summary
fields.what: LLM title and keyword-dense summary of the traces in the thread, no time information

write.how: one LLM call per session labels every numbered turn CHANGE_TOPIC or DEVELOP_TOPIC (looking two turns back and ahead) and writes a fact line per turn; the session is cut before each CHANGE_TOPIC
write.out: 925 episodes over the 10 LoCoMo conversations with GPT-4o-mini, 1,212 with GPT-4.1-mini
write.src: paper §3.1, Table 3; code segmenter.py L47-L116, prompts.py L1-L61

write.how: LLM rewrites the episode's turns into an exhaustive dated narrative
per speaker, LLM combines the summary with that speaker's fact lines and keeps only their own experiences, or returns N/A
write.src: paper §3.2, Table 3; code persona_extractor.py L40-L51, memory.py L114-L122

write.how: per user: PCA to at most 50 dims, UMAP to 2-D (cosine), HDBSCAN; noise points go to their best soft cluster or a KNN vote
same pipeline inside each topic; each thread's traces are joined and stored, and the LLM writes its title and summary
LLM titles each topic and the theme; theme, topics and threads (title, summary, id) are saved as one JSON card per user

read.how: LLM returns which user(s) the question is about (one or both)
read.src: paper §3.4; code agentic_search.py L15-L45, prompts.py L180-L206

read.scores: theme, topic and thread titles and thread summaries, read by the LLM
read.how: LLM returns relevant thread ids per user
text-embedding-3-small cosine search in the conversation's episode collection
look up each chosen thread id in the user's thread collection and take its stored text (joined traces)

answer_context.format:
"Question: ...

Contents:
Episodes:
<summaries, one per line>" then "<user> threads:
<thread texts>" per user
includes: 20 episode summaries in the code (10 in the paper)

compression.what: answer context vs one LoCoMo conversation
compression.basis: Not reported: the paper gives no context length, token or cost figures.

paper_vs_code.paper: agent examines titles, summaries and ids to pinpoint relevant threads
paper_vs_code.code: the prompt asks for exactly 10 thread ids per user and forbids an empty list

paper_vs_code.paper: threads group experiences that are semantically close and chronologically sequential
paper_vs_code.code: clusters on embeddings only (UMAP to 2-D, HDBSCAN); no time term

paper_vs_code.paper: cards chosen from user or topic cues in the query
paper_vs_code.code: an LLM chooses among the two speakers only

open_questions: The 'without agentic search' ablation is not specified further: it is unclear whether it drops the cards entirely or only the LLM thread selection, so the card structure and the LLM selection are not separated.
If the headline run used the code's 20 episodes, the gap to 'episodic memory only' (10 episodes, 84.29 vs 90.19) mixes more episodes with the added threads.
No baseline gets the same answer prompt, so how much of the lead over Nemori and LightMem comes from memory rather than from the answer prompt is not measured.

glance.a: Two kinds: an episode summary (an LLM rewrite of one topic segment, dated) and, per speaker, an experience trace of that speaker's own facts from the episode.
Yes. Episodes are stored only as LLM summaries told to omit nothing; the raw turns are not kept in memory.
Each user's traces are clustered into topics (HDBSCAN, min 5) and threads (min 2), written up as a JSON memory card: theme > topics > threads with titles, summaries and ids.
No. Episodes are taken in embedding order; threads are picked by an LLM that reads the whole card.

glance.q: Is memory reconstructed at question time?
glance.a: No second round: three LLM calls (pick card, pick threads, answer) and one embedding search per question.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: The episode summaries (20 in the code) and, for each chosen user, the joined experience traces of the selected threads. No original turns, fact lines or card summaries.

steps.what: thread ids named by the LLM

flow.title: Pick the user card(s)
flow.sees: Only the question and the two names.

flow.title: Choose threads from the card
flow.method: LLM reads the whole card JSON
flow.sees: Theme title, topic titles, and each thread's title, summary and id. Thread summaries carry no dates.

flow.title: Search episodes
flow.sees: Question vs each episode summary, embedded separately.

flow.title: Fetch thread texts
flow.sees: Each thread's stored text is its member traces joined together, each starting 'As of <date>'.

flow.title: Answer
flow.sees: Question, episode summaries, then per user the thread texts. Rules tell it to turn relative dates into absolute ones.

ablation.src: paper Table 4 (LoCoMo; the full row equals the GPT-4o-mini row of Table 2)

components.role: Clusters traces into topics and threads

discussion.takeaway: Turn dialogue into per-user narratives: summarise episodes, keep each speaker's own experiences, and cluster them into topic and thread cards that an LLM browses at question time. On LoCoMo this scores highest in the paper's own comparison, with the largest margins on multi-hop and temporal questions.

claims.claim: State of the art on LoCoMo across two backbones.
claims.evidence: Overall 90.19 (GPT-4o-mini) and 92.27 (GPT-4.1-mini) vs best baseline Nemori 74.03 and 80.52. Table 2, §4.2

claims.claim: Narrative threads help multi-hop and temporal reasoning.
claims.evidence: Multi-hop 92.20 vs 69.86 for full context (GPT-4o-mini); temporal 90.97 vs 81.62 full context (GPT-4.1-mini). §4.2

claims.claim: Consolidation beats simply adding more semantic facts.
claims.evidence: Episodes + 20/40 fact lines reach 87.01/87.92 overall vs 90.19 for the full system. Table 4, §4.3

claims.claim: Agentic search matters for multi-hop reasoning.
claims.evidence: Without it multi-hop falls 92.20 → 86.52 and overall 90.19 → 88.44, while open-domain rises to 71.88. Table 4

limits: The paper has no limitations section. Its open discussion names memory rewriting on recall, regulated forgetting, and deciding when to use memory at all as unaddressed.
Only LoCoMo is evaluated (the repo's LongMemEval folder holds only an empty readme).
reading: Full context scores 73.05 and 87.40 here while TraceMem scores 90.19 and 92.27, so the memory beats giving the model the whole conversation; the answer prompts differ, and the paper does not say which prompt the baselines used.
Fact lines (semantic memory) are stored in ChromaDB but read by no retrieval or answer code; they only feed trace distillation.
Thread summaries in the card carry no dates (the prompt forbids them), but the fetched thread text is the raw traces, which begin with 'As of <date>'.
The released code retrieves 20 episodes; the paper and its episodic-only ablation use 10.
No token, latency or cost figures are reported, although building cards adds per-user clustering and LLM titling after ingestion and each question needs three LLM calls.
Table 4 does not name its backbone; its full row matches the GPT-4o-mini numbers.

abstract.text: TraceMem builds long-term memory for dialogue agents by imitating memory consolidation. Each session is cut into topic episodes by an LLM that labels every turn, the episodes are summarised, and each speaker's own experiences are distilled from them. These experience traces are clustered per user into topics and threads and packaged as a structured memory card. At question time an LLM chooses cards and threads while dense search supplies episode summaries, and the authors report the best LoCoMo scores among their baselines with two GPT backbones.
